About

We love computers. We hate the part of the internet that only performs caring about them.

Tharavad is a public server for people who want a real box: a place to install things, break things, deploy something dumb at 2am, and learn without waiting for permission from a platform. It is not a course. It is not a vibe. It is hardware and software that still answers when you SSH in.

TinkerHub brought the iron

Credit where it is due: TinkerHub bought a server so we could mess with it without a five-year roadmap, then open the cycles to the community instead of hoarding a lonely lab toy. They supplied the cruft-free hardware. We frob the bits, mung the config until it boots, twiddle DNS and guests, and try not to lose the root partition on a Friday night.

The deal is simple and slightly unserious on purpose. Real metal and a public front door go in. Out comes a place where more than one nerd can have a shell. If that sounds like “we bought a box so people could have a playground,” yes. That is the gag, except the playground has SSH keys and git history instead of slides.

So when you land a VM here, you are not on a private vanity rack. You are on infrastructure TinkerHub was willing to fund so the learning stays hands-on: less slide deck, more ssh, more “why is this unit failed,” more shipping something small that actually runs.

Where we are

The default internet today is rented. Your “server” is someone else’s control panel. Your “community” is a feed optimized to keep you scrolling. Tutorials are infinite, and so is noise. A lot of people who could have become dangerous with a shell never get past a signup wall, a credit card, or the feeling that the real rooms are closed.

That is a waste. The tools are better than ever. What is scarce is a place that treats you like a peer instead of a user metric. Forums used to do that. University labs used to do that. This is one more corner.

What we can do here

  • Get a real NixOS guest under your name, not a line in someone else’s passwd file.
  • SSH from anywhere with a normal key: you@you.tharavad.xyz.
  • Publish a small service if you want: https://you.tharavad.xyz on a port you declare in git.
  • Leave a trail that matters: membership is a PR. The history is readable.

Longer rants live under Notes so this page stays a door, not a dump. Start with People we stand on, On HTTP, and Back to HTTPS.

Membership is boring on purpose. You open a pull request with your SSH key. Someone reviews it. After merge, you get a guest under your name. Your mess stays in your guest. Shape of the machine: mothership. Shell: Join.
